speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a postmenopausal woman presenting with vaginal bleeding and an adnexal mass; please know that while the bleeding is concerning, our priority is to determine the cause of both findings safely. To begin, is your bleeding heavy enough to require changing your pad more often than every hour, and have you experienced any dizziness or fainting spells?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since you are a 65-year-old woman with intermittent bleeding but no signs of acute instability, I need to characterize the adnexal mass. Can you tell me the size of the mass found on your exam and whether it causes any pain, and did your physician order any imaging like an ultrasound or CT scan?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial hyperplasia or endometrial carcinoma with concurrent benign ovarian cyst.
The history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding in a 65-year-old woman is highly suspicious for uterine pathology, and the adnexal mass requires characterization to rule out malignancy.
REQUEST TEST: Transvaginal_Ultrasound (to assess endometrial thickness and characterize the adnexal mass).
